steps.en: What you see: The descending aorta sits as a clean circle behind the airway with the spine shadow beyond. A dissection flap crosses the circle as a bright line that flutters independently of the wall.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Measurements and worked gradients: Report maximum diameter in millimetres with the segment named, since size drives referral.
Pressure drop in mmHg equals 4 times the peak velocity in m per s squared.
A tricuspid velocity of 3.5 m per s gives 4 times 3.5 squared, which is 49 mmHg, plus right atrial pressure.
Tricuspid regurgitation peak velocity 2.8 m per s or less is normal.

Pitfalls: Reverberation from the near wall can paint a false second line; a true flap moves with its own rhythm and shows different Doppler each side. Never clear the aorta from one plane; arch, ascending and abdominal segments each need their own look.

spot.en: Common mistakes and how to correct them: Mistaking the transverse arch for the descending aorta. Correct it by following the vessel down, since the arch curves away while the descending runs straight.
Azygos arch mimicking a second lumen. Correct it by tracking the extra vessel, since the azygos joins the cava and never runs the full length.
Rotation that turns the circle into an oval and fakes a flap. Correct it by rotating back until the vessel is round before judging the lumen.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at suprasternal notch, transverse tilted left with neck extended.
Point the probe marker toward the left shoulder, about two o clock.
From the arch long axis, rotate ninety degrees and tilt left until the vessel is a circle, not an oval. Any oval means obliquity that can fake a flap.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Measure the descending aorta for surveillance.

q.en: The vessel reads as an oval. What do you do?

o.en: Rotate back until it is round, since ovals fake flaps

why.en: Obliquity turns circles to ovals and paints false flaps.

q.en: Tricuspid velocity is 3 m per s with right atrial pressure 8 mmHg. What is pulmonary systolic pressure?

why.en: Four times nine is 36, plus 8 gives 44 mmHg.

q.en: A bright line flutters inside the circle with different Doppler each side. What is this?

why.en: Independent motion with its own Doppler marks a true flap.

q.en: Near wall reverberation paints a second line that moves with the wall. What is this?

why.en: A line that moves exactly with the wall is reverberation artefact.
